facts.text: In the clean-butterknife-to-drawer pair, drawer 1 was opened and contained a knife 1 and a spatula 1; no butterknife is shown at that location in either run.
Parent took the near-match knife 1, cleaned it at sinkbasin 1, and moved it to drawer 1.
Parent continued searching after placing the knife and hit the step limit; Candidate left the knife untouched, kept visiting drawers/cabinets/countertops, and also hit the step limit.
Memory M11 records this pair as support that the strengthened exact-category rule stops ineffective near-match manipulation but does not create success when the exact target is absent.

answers.conditions: One trial per side; detailed windows are partial (P7:12-47 and Q7:5-47 omitted); the two runs are separate executions of the same task.
answers.comparison: Parent acquired and conditioned a near-match knife; Candidate refused the knife and kept searching. Neither located an exact butterknife before the 50-step budget expired.
answers.conclusion: Both S1_R05/P7 and S1_R05/Q7 failed with step_limit. The evidence supports that the exact-category rule prevented cleaning/placing the knife, but it neither produced nor guaranteed success, since no butterknife was found in either run.
answers.uncertainty: The unobserved middle steps are missing, so global absence of a butterknife is not proven—only that it was not located within the budget. Availability may differ across instances and results are single-trial.

facts.text: Parent took plate 3 from countertop 3, then inserted it into the microwave, closed and reopened the door, took it out, heated it while holding, and moved it to cabinet 1; success in 13 steps.
Candidate cycled among countertop 1, cabinets 1-6 and drawer 1, never reached countertop 3, and ended at the 50-step limit with success=false.
The S1_R04 edit added temperature-conditioned placement wording requiring conditioning on the held target without door toggling; M7 cites S1_R04/P2:13 and Q2:50 for this pair.

answers.conditions: One trial per side on the heat-a-plate-to-cabinet task; Candidate windows omit Q2:1-47; no step alignment exists between the two runs.
answers.comparison: Parent acquired the exact plate and applied conditioning (with insertion/toggling), succeeding in 13 steps; Candidate never acquired the target and failed before any conditioning opportunity.
answers.conclusion: The Parent's success versus the Candidate's step-limit failure supports M7's claim that temperature guidance yields savings conditional on locating the exact target; here the edit had no chance to act.
answers.uncertainty: Candidate's omitted middle steps and possible instance-level target-location variation mean the failure cannot be attributed to the edit; single runs limit inference.

facts.text: Parent opened the fridge (empty), revisited countertop 1 and cabinet 1, examined toaster 1, and only acquired tomato 1 on countertop 2 at step 13, finishing in 18 steps.

Candidate opened the fridge, checked countertop 1 then countertop 2, took tomato 1 at step 5, cooled it while holding at fridge 1 at step 7, then went to the microwave, opened it, and moved the tomato in at step 10.
Parent likewise cooled tomato 1 while holding at the fridge (step 15) and placed it by opening the microwave (steps 17-18).

answers.conditions: Current pair P2/Q2, task 'put a cool tomato in microwave' (val:0012); single execution per side; guidance changes are the current diff (single-pass sweep, exact-category, direct conditioning wording).
answers.comparison: Search: Parent 13 steps with cabinet/toaster revisits; Candidate 5 steps. Conditioning: both performed cool-tomato-with-fridge while holding, without inserting it. Placement: both opened the microwave and moved the tomato in. Totals 18 vs 10.
answers.conclusion: Acquisition conditioning and placement behavior are preserved (direct held cooling, one-shot microwave placement), while Candidate used 8 fewer steps, mainly from shorter search; consistent with, but not solely attributable to, the guidance edits.
answers.uncertainty: Single runs, no step alignment, and multiple simultaneous guidance changes prevent isolating the search wording as the cause of the step reduction.
